finding.title: Stop catching StateError (an Error subtype) in user_profile_dao.dart's AccountX.accountTier getter
finding.why: `StateError` extends `Error` in dart:core, and `UserTierX.fromDb` throws it specifically for an unrecognized `tier` string — i.e. local DB corruption or a missed enum-value migration. Catching it here and silently returning `UserTier.localBorn` masks that bug: a `cloudBorn` account whose stored tier string ever drifts (bad migration, hand-edited row, future enum rename) silently behaves as local-born everywhere accountTier is read (sync gating, balance-row eligibility per 'Adults never have balance rows (Rule 3)', etc.), with nothing logged.
finding.recommendation: Let the StateError propagate (or catch and rethrow after an AppLogger.error call) instead of returning a silent fallback — an unrecognized tier value is a bug that should be loud, not a normal control-flow case.
acceptance_criteria: AccountX.accountTier no longer has an `on StateError` handler that returns a default value.
A test asserts that an Account row with an unrecognized `tier` string causes accountTier to throw (or to log via AppLogger and rethrow), not silently return localBorn.

finding.title: Replace human-readable English StateError messages with stable codes in the DAO layer

evidence.quote:
throw StateError(
        'Cannot deactivate the last active curriculum for this profile',

throw StateError(
        'INSERT OR IGNORE collided but the companion has no ulid set — '
'Cannot seed study day defaults: curriculum_tracks row $trackId not found',

finding.why: All four throw a plain English sentence instead of a stable code/enum. EH-5 exists because this is an EN+Hebrew app — if any of these ever reaches presentation (a catch-and-display-e.toString() somewhere upstream, or a crash reporter surfaced to a bilingual support flow), the message renders untranslated English with no ARB key to localize it.
finding.recommendation: Introduce a small typed error (e.g. sealed DaoError with named variants, or a code enum carried on a custom Exception) for these four call sites; have callers map codes to AppLocalizations strings at the presentation boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The 4 sites throw a typed/coded error instead of a raw English StateError string.
A grep-based Rule-0 check (e.g. `grep -rn "StateError('[A-Z]" lib/core/database/`) is added to catch new pre-formatted messages in the DAO layer.

finding.title: Replace track_dao.dart's stringly-typed TrackState class with a real Dart enum
finding.why: TrackState is a 4-value closed lifecycle (active/retired/archived/deleted) central to this HOTSPOT file's whole model, modeled as bare String constants on a TextColumn with no DB-level or compiler-level check that only these 4 values ever get stored. Any code that branches on `.state` gets no exhaustiveness checking, and nothing stops a typo'd string reaching the column (mitigated today only by everyone remembering to use the TrackState.* constants rather than literals — a convention, not a guarantee).
finding.recommendation: Model TrackState as a real Dart `enum` (or use Drift's `.withConverter` to store it as text but expose an enum in Dart), so switches over track state are compiler-exhaustive and no non-member string can be constructed.
acceptance_criteria: TrackState is a Dart enum (or enum-backed column); all TrackState.active-style call sites in this batch keep compiling.
Any switch/when over the state value is exhaustive without a default/_ arm.

finding.title: Fix test groups in completion_dao_extended_test.dart and completion_dao_extra_test.dart that reference the removed CompletionDao.insertCompletionsBatch method
finding.why: completion_dao.dart's own doc comment states: 'Write methods (insertCompletion, insertCompletionsBatch) have been removed. New completions are written exclusively through CompletionWriter.' These two group() blocks (and completion_dao_extended_test.dart's file-header doc comment) still name and describe `CompletionDao.insertCompletionsBatch` as if it exists. What they actually exercise is the test-only `seedCompletionsBatch` helper (test/helpers/drift_memory.dart, itself an unbatched loop over `completionEventDao.appendEvent`) followed by CompletionDao read methods. A future maintainer reading these group names would reasonably believe CompletionDao still exposes a batch-insert API.
finding.recommendation: Rename the groups/comments to describe what's actually under test (e.g. 'seeding + getCompletionsByTrack/ByProfile') or drop the stale 'insertCompletionsBatch' framing entirely.
acceptance_criteria: Neither file's group()/doc-comment names a CompletionDao method that doesn't exist on the class.

finding.title: De-duplicate near-identical CompletionDao test coverage between completion_dao_extended_test.dart and completion_dao_extra_test.dart
finding.why: Both files were independently written against 'the baseline test' (each file's header says so) and ended up covering the same 5 methods — insertCompletionsBatch(seed helper), getCompletionsByTrackAndProfile, getAggregateCountByTrack, completionExistsByTrack, getCompletionsByDateRangeAndTrack — with near-identical happy-path/profile-scoping/empty-list scenarios. Neither file references the other. This doubles maintenance cost (a behavior change requires updating matching assertions in two places) for zero added coverage on 5 of the two files' groups; completion_dao_review_counts_test.dart by contrast adds real net-new scenarios (track/profile/ref filter edge cases) alongside minor overlap, so it's not implicated here.
finding.recommendation: Merge the 5 overlapping groups into one file (extra_test.dart's cases look like a strict subset of extended_test.dart's), or add a comment in the newer file cross-referencing the older one so future authors know not to add a third copy.
acceptance_criteria: The 5 duplicated method groups exist in exactly one file, or the newer file documents what it adds beyond the older one.
Total assertion count for these 5 methods is unchanged or increased (dedup must not drop coverage).
